## TL;DR

Work is now the home page. Opening `/`, the Hub's start URL, or an unknown path lands on `/work`. Mission Control moved to `/control`. On phone widths the routed page's scrollbar is hidden and the reclaimed right padding is removed, so the gutters match. Every header-row control reads one height token (30px desktop, 44px at 900px and below), and the project chip is a stadium with heavier, larger text. Headless WebKit tests cover heights at 375, 412, 768 and 1280 px in both themes, the gutters, and the default route. Nothing was run on a real Android device, so touch feel and the Hub's start behaviour on a phone are unverified.

## Work and rationale

**Default route.** The root path was the Control dashboard, so the fix had to move Control off `/`. I made `/` a redirect to `/work` and gave Control `/control`. Redirecting `/` is the only change that covers every entry point at once: the browser root, the Hub (which loads the server root), the login return path, and the catch-all for unknown paths. The nav entry and the loading skeleton (`/control` gets the dashboard shape, `/` the board shape) were updated to match. Deep links such as `/work?task=…` keep their query. I checked the docs for places that describe Control as the home page; the only one that named `/` for the live activity view was the mobile ADR, which I updated. The dated QA and audit notes keep their original `/` references because they describe the app at their date.

**Scrollbar and gutters.** On phones the routed page is the scroller, and the global 8px webkit scrollbar sat on its right edge. I hid it with `scrollbar-width: none` and `::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none }` for `.main > :not(.spin)`, under the 719.98px query. Two pages (`.page-scroll-body`, `.agents-tab-content`) reserved 3px of right padding for that bar. On phones that padding made the right gutter wider than the left, so I zeroed it there. The rules sit at the end of `style.css`, because the stylesheet's own comment notes that later base rules would otherwise beat a phone override placed earlier. Desktop rules are untouched.

**Header row.** The phone header had mixed heights from separate per-control overrides spread over several breakpoints. I replaced them with one custom property, `--topbar-control-h`, set on `.topbar` (30px, and 44px inside the existing 900px touch block). The project chip, search field, bell, theme toggle, help and account triggers all read it. The chip also gets `border-radius: 999px` to match the search field, `font-size: 13px`, weight 600, and weight 700 on the project name. Colours all come from existing theme tokens.

**Tests.** `mobile-header-scroll-browser.test.ts` loads the real `style.css` plus the TopBar and NoticeBell scoped styles in headless WebKit on mirrored markup. It checks computed heights and vertical centre for all six controls at four widths and both themes, the chip's radius and type, the zeroed right padding, equal gutters at 375 and 412, and that the scroller still scrolls. `home-route-work.test.ts` uses the real router. I updated `router-guard.test.ts`, since the login return path is now `/work`, and `app-loading-skeleton.test.ts` for the new skeleton keys.

## Approaches tried

I first assumed the phone chip was taller than the round buttons because of its 44px minimum. Reading the CSS showed most phone controls were already 44px, so the mismatch was partly a cascade problem and partly the desktop 30px sizes. A single token fixes both without guessing which breakpoint wins, and the browser test checks the result rather than the CSS values.

For the scrollbar I first wanted to assert the bar's own width in the browser test. A quick measurement showed headless WebKit draws no bar even without the rule (`offsetWidth - clientWidth` is 0), so that assertion could never fail. I replaced it with an assertion on the padding and gutter effect, which the rule does change, and added a stylesheet check that always runs and pins the rule.

## Challenges and blockers

**Remote gate failed on a different host.** `repoos check` ran its tests on the remote runner `thinkpad`. The only failure there was `ui-smoke`, with three console errors: a failed preconnect to `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com`, and a WebKit internal error loading `manifest.webmanifest`. The smoke step has no benign-URL filter (the page gate in `src/core/page-browser-gate.ts` does), so an offline host fails it. My diff does not touch `index.html`, the manifest, or any font. The same script passed on my machine after a full `bun run build`, with the same change set. This points to the remote host's network and WebKit, but I have not confirmed it on that host.

**Local gate result.** `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check --local-tests` passed on this machine (all steps, exit 0), including the scoped test pass. The remote run is the only failing gate, and it is the host problem above.

**Build order.** `scripts/ui-smoke.mjs` needs the compiled CLI in `dist/`, so running it right after `build:ui` fails with "dist/commands/ui-smoke.js not found". A full `bun run build` is needed first.

**Files changed under me.** The edit tool twice reported that a test file had changed on disk between my reads. Both times the change was my own scripted edit, and `git status` showed only the intended paths.

## Key learnings

- A CSS token on the header row is easier to keep consistent than per-breakpoint overrides, and a computed-height test catches drift.
- Headless WebKit hides overlay scrollbars, so a test should assert the layout effect (padding, gutters) and pin the rule in the stylesheet, not assert a bar width that cannot be measured.
- Making `/` a redirect rather than moving the component keeps every entry point (the Hub's start URL, the login return path, unknown paths) on one rule. The cost is that Control needs its own path, which the nav, skeleton and ADR had to follow.
- The remote gate's ui-smoke is stricter about console errors than the page gate, so a host without internet access can fail a change that is fine locally. That is an environment problem to fix on the host, not in the code.
